title: First US Deportation Flight Since TPS Termination Lands 161 in Cap-Haïtien
detail: The US deported more than 160 Haitians on a charter flight that departed an ICE hub in Alexandria, Louisiana and landed at Cap-Haïtien International Airport on August 20, 2026 — the first mass deportation flight since the Trump administration secured Supreme Court clearance to terminate Temporary Protected Status for roughly 350,000 Haitians, effective July 26, 2026. The flight bypassed Port-au-Prince because its main airport remains closed to commercial traffic under a US flight ban through early September due to gang violence that controls an estimated 70% of the capital; Haiti's migration office director Jean Négot Bonheur Delva said arriving deportees would be offered up to $65, food, and temporary shelter. Deportee Jean Diane Louis told reporters ICE 'took me without questioning me. They just sent me here,' while advocacy groups including Haiti's Group Supporting Refugees said the country 'is not ready to receive this number of migrants' amid 1.5 million already displaced by gang violence nationwide. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul sent a same-day letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin calling the TPS termination a 'reckless and inhumane act' and warning New York would be forced to fire hundreds of essential Haitian and Salvadoran government workers by August 24.

media.caption: Deportees arrive at Cap-Haïtien International Airport on the first US removal flight since Haitian TPS ended

title: Haiti's CEP Opens Candidate Registration for December 13 Elections
detail: Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) opened registration for presidential and legislative candidates on August 20, 2026, holding an exchange session at the Kinam Hotel in Port-au-Prince to present its online candidate-registration platform to representatives of the 228 approved political parties and platforms and train system administrators designated by those organizations. The registration window runs through October 2, 2026, ahead of a campaign period from October 5 to December 12 and the first-round vote on December 13 — Haiti's first national election in a decade. The CEP has repeatedly stressed the electoral timetable depends on an 'acceptable security environment,' with armed groups controlling an estimated 70-90% of the capital and voter registration lagging (roughly 260,000 registered as of OAS Secretary General Albert Ramdin's August 19 visit) amid nearly 1.5 million Haitians displaced by gang violence.
